newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Monday with money supply ample due to the recent heavy redemption of matured state debt, traders said.
But the rate for the most active three-day contract soared to 9.50 percent from 2.90 percent on a technical rebound after a fall last Friday, they said.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 6.6 million lots from 5.1 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
China is facing a state debt redemption peak in 1997 with more than 120 billion yuan worth of state debt maturing, the bulk between April and June.
"Heavy redemption of matured state debt is driving large amounts of money into the repo market," one trader said. "This has helped depress the repo rates in the past five trading days."
Trading was a little more active than last Friday in line with the strong performance on the A share markets, traders said.
"The rates are likely to see some rises on Tuesday after five days of losses in a row given the fact that there is a new issue on A share market," said a second trader.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Monday on profit-taking after successive gains in the past few days, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 117.64 yuan from 118.15 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.3 million lots from 1.9 million lots.

Despite today's fall, traders said market sentiment was good as a result of the fresh liquidity being injected into the market from the redeemed state debt, and spot prices were likely to rise in the short term.
